subject.title: fix(github-copilot): reject unsupported OAuth enterprise domain before refresh and model routing

question: Should legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth credentials with an unsupported persisted enterprise origin be refused for both refresh and model routing, while credentials from github.com or a single-label *.ghe.com tenant may continue trusting their token-provided proxy endpoint?
rationale: The code can enforce this boundary cleanly, but choosing which credential origins and token metadata OpenClaw permanently trusts—and intentionally breaking unsupported legacy profiles—requires provider/security-owner authority.

options.title: Confirm fail-closed boundary
options.body: Approve the allowlist and re-authentication behavior as the permanent legacy-profile security and upgrade contract, then merge after rebasing and required checks.

options.title: Require broader upgrade proof
options.body: Ask for explicit multi-profile and end-to-end re-authentication proof before accepting the intentional legacy-profile break.

options.title: Retire the legacy path
options.body: Pause this PR and remove or migrate the executable legacy OAuth provider through a separately owned compatibility plan instead.

recommendation.title: Confirm fail-closed boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the allowlist and re-authentication behavior as the permanent legacy-profile security and upgrade contract, then merge after rebasing and required checks.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work is closest to GitHub Copilot token exchange, provider endpoints, and plugin ownership, which are the central trust surfaces in this decision.
